summary: Surveyed the checkout (arademaker__fad, at reservoir-sources/arademaker__fad): confirmed all 4 review-list files exist under Fad/. This is a machine-checked formalization of the textbook 'Functional Algorithm Design' (quicksort/mergesort correctness, symmetric lists, binary search trees, foldr1/minimum/maximum, and running-time/complexity results via a TimeM monad), consistent with the prior review RRV-b4b877bc383f-r1's summary. Read the head of every file (imports, namespace, first section): Chapter3-Ex.lean and Chapter5-Ex.lean are numbered textbook-exercise files (`# Exercicio 3.1`, `# Exercicio 5.2`, etc.) proving properties of the chapter's definitions via `example`/`theorem`; Chapter5.lean defines the chapter's own algorithms (`Tree`, quicksort, mergesort) and their correctness lemmas; Chapter6.lean imports `Cslib.Algorithms.Lean.TimeM` alongside the earlier chapters and proves both correctness (`maximum_eq_foldrmax`, `minimum_eq_foldrmin`) and running-time properties of `foldr1`/`minimum`/`maximum` and related algorithms. Ran \bsorry\b, \badmit\b, and TODO/FIXME/XXX greps over all 4 files: `admit` and TODO/FIXME/XXX had zero matches in every file; `sorry` had zero matches in three files and exactly one match in Fad/Chapter5-Ex.lean (line 153). Read the sorry's context (lines 143-153): it closes one case of an `example (xs : List Nat) : msort₂ xs = msort₃ xs := by induction ... | cons x xs ih => simp [msort₂, msort₃]; sorry` inside 'Exercicio 5.9' -- a genuine but isolated incomplete proof of one specific example, inside a file that otherwise carries 51 total declaration-keyword matches including several other complete, non-trivial induction proofs in the same section (e.g. the T a b ≤ a + b lemma immediately preceding it, read in full at lines 100-136). Per the precedent established earlier this session (or4nge19__MCMC, YaelDillies__mean-fourier), an isolated incomplete proof of one exercise inside an otherwise declaration-rich file is not a content-level reason under FILTER-002/004 to exclude the file; the file's other completed theorems/examples remain genuine searchable formal-mathematics content. No stub, data dump, or placeholder found anywhere in the unit. No exclusions.
